claim: GPU-to-GPU P2P works on the CMP 170HX over BAR1 P2P (not the mailbox), measured at 1.68 GB/s each way on PCIe Gen2 x4 with a full 4-GPU mesh of 12/12 directed pairs verified with real transfers rather than cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer().
stance_target: the repo's claim that P2P is impossible on this hardware and therefore that every topology requiring peer traffic is ruled out by the fabric
scope_conditions: Four CMP 170HX behind one PLX switch on SYS-4028GR-TRT2, PCIe Gen2 x4, BAR1-P2P driver patches applied, RMForceStaticBar1=1 and RMPcieP2PType=1
quoted_support: P2P works, over **BAR1 P2P** — not the mailbox. Measured **1.68 GB/s** each way on PCIe Gen2 x4, full 4-GPU mesh (12/12 directed pairs), verified with real transfers rather than `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer()`.

claim: The GA100 PCIe write-mailbox P2P path is a documented dead end on these cards: the driver configures it correctly, both GSP RPCs return NV_OK, the mailbox BAR1 area is allocated, and transfers still move exactly zero bytes with no error and no Xid.
stance_target: why a naive 'just enable P2P' attempt on this card fails silently and is mistaken for a hardware limitation
quoted_support: On these cards the driver configures it correctly — the connection type is chosen, both GSP RPCs return `NV_OK`, the mailbox BAR1 area is allocated — and transfers still move exactly zero bytes, with no error and no Xid. Hours went into that path before concluding it is not recoverable in software.

claim: All CMP 170HX cards report x4 (downgraded) from an x16 capability, and that x4 is normal while x2 is not: one card that trained at x2 ran exactly half speed everywhere (0.84 GB/s same-switch, ~0.58 GB/s cross-switch) with zero AER correctable errors.
stance_target: the repo's 'PCIe Gen2 x4' premise — x4 is the normal negotiated width for this card, and it is a physical (riser/seating/contamination) property rather than signal integrity under load
scope_conditions: Eight CMP 170HX across two PLX switches on one Xeon E5 v4 root complex; LnkSta Width x2 against LnkCap x16
quoted_support: All CMP 170HX report `x4 (downgraded)` from an x16 capability; that x4 is normal, x2 is not. ... One card trained at x2 instead of x4 and was exactly half speed everywhere (0.84 GB/s same-switch, ~0.58 cross). `LnkSta` said `Width x2` against a `LnkCap` of x16, with **zero** AER correctable errors

claim: Scaling to eight GPUs across two PLX switches on one Xeon E5 v4 root complex, all 56 directed pairs pass an alias-proof P2P test including all 32 cross-switch pairs, with same-switch pairs at a uniform 1.68 GB/s and cross-switch at 1.07-1.45 GB/s (~78% of same-switch).
stance_target: the assumption that cross-root-complex P2P is unsupported on this platform — NVIDIA's own gate rates it unsupported but empirically it works
scope_conditions: Eight CMP 170HX, four behind each of two PLX switches on the same CPU root complex, Xeon E5 v4 (cpuType=0x8), ACS redirection disabled on every port of both switches
quoted_support: All 56 directed pairs pass the alias-proof test — real peer reads _and_ real peer writes, no local aliasing — including all 32 cross-switch pairs. ... same-switch  : 18 pairs, all 1.68 GB/s / cross-switch : 24 pairs, 1.07-1.45 GB/s  (~78% of same-switch)

claim: ACS redirection must be disabled on every port of both switches: leaving switch A with ReqRedir+/CmpltRedir+ forced same-switch peer traffic up to the root complex and back, dropping same-switch bandwidth from 1.68 to 1.20 GB/s while still working correctly.
stance_target: the operational precondition for getting the measured P2P bandwidth — a silent 29% performance loss otherwise
scope_conditions: Two PLX switches, pci=disable_acs_redir listing all ports of both switches including empty slots; verify with lspci -vv | grep ACSCtl
quoted_support: Switch A came up with `ReqRedir+ CmpltRedir+`, which forces peer traffic up to the root complex and back even between two GPUs on the _same_ switch. It still works — it is a performance bug, not a correctness one, which is exactly why it is easy to miss: | same-switch A | 1.20 GB/s | **1.68 GB/s** |

claim: BAR1 P2P requires all of the following together: patches 0011 (BAR1 P2P HALs forced on for Ampere plus peer-PTE rewrite), 0013 (skip mailbox peer pre-registration), 0015 (restore the BAR1-P2P read cap), kernel patches for a 64 GB BAR1 from a normal boot, and RMForceStaticBar1=1 plus RMPcieP2PType=1 in modprobe.d followed by update-initramfs.
stance_target: the cost of enabling P2P — it is a five-part patch set, not a flag, which is why the repo's 'no P2P' claim is a reasonable default-state observation but not a hardware limit
scope_conditions: nvidia-open driver with cmpunlocker fork; module parameters must be followed by update-initramfs -u because nvidia loads from the initramfs
quoted_support: All of these, together: | BAR1 P2P HALs forced on for Ampere + peer-PTE rewrite | `driver/patches/0011-p2p-bar1.patch` | ... | `RMForceStaticBar1=1` and `RMPcieP2PType=1` | `/etc/modprobe.d` + `update-initramfs -u` |
numbers: 3 driver patches + kernel patches + 2 module params

claim: The unlock restores full SM compute, memory geometry (64 GB on 8 GB cards, 40 GB on 10 GB cards), PCIe Gen2, BAR1 64 MB -> 64 GB and HBM2e NDIV overclock, but not NVLink or ECC.
stance_target: the repo's hardware table: 64 GB per card and Gen2 are achievable, NVLink is not
scope_conditions: nvidia-open 610.43.03 or 610.43.02, Linux x86-64/aarch64, root, Secure Boot disabled, cold reboot required
quoted_support: | Full SM compute throughput (SS0/SS1)  | Working  | | Memory geometry (64GB on 8GB cards, 40GB on 10GB cards)  | Working  | | PCIe Gen 2 speeds  | Working  | | GPU-to-GPU P2P (`cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess`)  | Working (BAR1 P2P, needs kernel patches — see below)  | | BAR1 64mb->64gb (requires Above 4G Decoding in BIOS)  | Working  |

claim: HBM2e clock is set by the FBPA PLL multiplier N, giving N x 27 MHz: stock is NDIV 54 (1,458 MHz) on the 250 W 8 GB VBIOS and NDIV 64 (1,728 MHz) on the 300 W VBIOS, with NDIV 70 (1,890 MHz) working on about 60% of 8 GB cards and NDIV 73 usually only on lucky cards.
stance_target: the memory-bandwidth headroom available to a training run, since decode and prefill on this card are HBM-bound
scope_conditions: Both 0x20C2 (8 GB) and 0x2082 (10 GB) SKUs; --mclk-ndiv compiled into the modules; values below stock downclock and are the way to stabilise a failing card
quoted_support: `--mclk-ndiv=N` sets the FBPA PLL multiplier; the resulting clock is `N * 27` MHz. ... | 54  | 1458 MHz  | Stock 8gb 250w vbios  | | 64  | 1728 MHz  | Stock 8gb 300w vbios  | | 70  | 1890 MHz  | Works on ~60% of 8gb cards  | | 73  | 1971 MHz  | Usually only on lucky 8gb cards  |

claim: Two operations reliably hang the machine and cost a hard power cycle: the ForceP2P=0x11 registry dword, and unloading/re-inserting the nvidia module on a live system.
stance_target: the operational risk profile of iterating on driver patches for a training rig — a failed experiment can take the whole box down
scope_conditions: CMP 170HX with the cmpunlocker fork; apply module parameters via /etc/modprobe.d + initramfs rebuild + reboot
quoted_support: Both cost a hard power cycle, TTY included: * `NVreg_RegistryDwords="ForceP2P=0x11"`. * Unloading and re-inserting the nvidia module on a live system.
